findings.title: Removing the full BuildIndex lock allows concurrent duplicate builds of the same index
findings.body: Previously `BuildIndex` held `cacheMu` for the whole function, which (coarsely) guaranteed only one build per key ran at a time and that a cache entry existed before another `GetIndex`/`BuildIndex` could proceed. Now the lock is only taken around the final cache write. `resource.getOrCreateIndex` has no per-key synchronization (its own TODO admits this): two concurrent Search requests for a namespace whose index is not yet cached will both see `GetIndex` return nil and both call `BuildIndex` concurrently. For indexes above the file threshold, both goroutines call `bleve.New` on the same directory; the second one fails (bleve refuses to create an index in an existing path), so the request returns an error, and the two half-built indexes can also clobber each other in `b.cache`. The fix needs a per-key singleflight/mutex, not just moving the lock.

findings.title: Data race on shared err variable and totalBatchesIndexed in concurrent index build
findings.body: In `init`, the worker goroutines launched via `group.Go` all assign to the captured outer `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increment `totalBatchesIndexed` without any synchronization. Since this PR explicitly increases concurrency of index builds (worker pool plus finer-grained bleve locking), these unsynchronized writes are now a genuine data race (Go race detector will flag it; a lost or torn error value can mask build failures, and the `namespaced_indexed` span attribute can be wrong). Each goroutine should use its own local err, and the counter should be atomic or accumulated from return values.

findings.title: Constructor does not clean up on Init failure
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure, but never calls `s.cancel()` or `s.Stop(ctx)`. If the failure happens after lifecycle hooks ran (lifecycle.Init may have started resources) or after `searchSupport.init` started its watch-event goroutine, the cancellable context and any goroutines started during partial init are leaked. On the error path the constructor should tear down what was started (at minimum `s.cancel()`).

findings.title: Watch-event goroutine panics on nil event when the events channel is closed
findings.body: The goroutine started in `init` does `v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v)` with no `ok` check and no loop-exit condition. The SQL backend's poller closes the stream channel when the backend is stopped (`b.cancel()` in `Stop`). After the channel is closed, `<-events` yields a nil `*WrittenEvent`, and `handleEvent` immediately dereferences `evt.Type`, panicking the process. Additionally the goroutine uses `context.Background()`, so it is never terminated on shutdown. It should check `evt, ok := <-events; if !ok { return }` and use a cancellable context tied to server shutdown.

findings.title: Postgres variant of the integration test is silently skipped with a TODO
findings.body: The only change to this test is skipping postgres entirely ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally'). This removes coverage for the storage server target on one of the two supported databases with no tracking issue referenced, so a postgres-only regression in unified storage startup (which this PR makes eager via `NewResourceServer`) would go undetected. Either link the TODO to an issue or fix the Drone environment so the coverage is not silently lost.
